# Rust review rules

Read by the Codex `rust-pr-review` skill. Adapt the project policy below before
using this template as a merge gate. Existing repository contracts take precedence.

## Severity

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Proven critical defect with broad impact: memory unsoundness, data destruction or secret disclosure |
| P1 | Reachable regression, broken contract, deadlock or other defect that must be fixed before merge |
| P2 | Concrete non-blocking correctness, maintainability or measured performance issue |
| P3 | Optional actionable improvement; omit taste-only comments |

Determine priority from reachability, impact and preconditions. A panic, unsafe block,
clone, lint violation or failing command does not automatically establish P0/P1.
Distinguish environment failures and pre-existing failures from defects in the diff.
Each finding needs an exact location, trigger, impact and practical fix. For a deletion,
identify its base-side location explicitly; never invent a current line for missing code.

## Project policy (configure)

- Use the actual edition, MSRV, toolchain, lint levels and error conventions in this repo.
- Review public API compatibility against the project's supported release baseline.
- Check unsafe invariants, aliasing/lifetimes, ownership across FFI and Send/Sync claims.
- Check async blocking, lock order, cancellation, bounded resource use and error paths.
- Require tests for meaningful behavior changes where they protect against regressions.
- Default checks: fmt, clippy, tests (including doctests), cargo-deny with deny.toml.
- Default feature configuration: --all-features. Replace with the supported feature
  matrix for mutually exclusive features; align local checks and CI.
- Configure deny.toml using the project's license, advisory and source policy.
- Only mark deny N/A if project policy explicitly makes it inapplicable; missing
  cargo-deny or deny.toml means NOT RUN. If required evidence is absent, INCOMPLETE.
- Spec PASS requires user requirements or PR acceptance criteria; commit claims alone
  yield PARTIAL. No findings does not mean all requirements were verified.
- For affected unsafe/FFI boundaries, targeted Miri tests and a separate aliasing/
  provenance argument are required before approval. Use isolated exact-source probes
  when existing tests do not cover the path and execution is authorized. Unknown FFI
  guarantees, unavailable targeted execution or conflicting alias models require ESCALATE.
  General tests passing under Miri are not a substitute. Follow the skill’s
  references/MEMORY-VALIDATION.md and report the Memory safety section.
- For affected async behavior, require targeted progress/deadlock, cancellation and
  task-termination tests as applicable. For changed custom synchronization protocols,
  require Loom models and an independent invariant/ordering argument. Missing relevant
  evidence or incomplete models require ESCALATE. Follow references/CONCURRENCY-VALIDATION.md
  and report the Concurrency section; green ordinary tests are not a substitute.
- Semver-checks remain conditional; document applicability and skipped checks.

The skill provides smell, safety and spec references under
`.agents/skills/rust-pr-review/references/`. They inform judgment and do not override
verified source, repository policy or explicit user instructions.

## Fixture project policy

This is an unpublished crate with no dependencies. Required checks: fmt, clippy,
unit tests, doctests and cargo-deny. Requirements are in REQUIREMENTS.md.
No Miri or semver-checks gate applies (no unsafe code; publish=false).

Run diagnostics offline using the existing toolchains and advisory database. Record this freshness limitation. Use equivalent offline gate commands if necessary. Do not install dependencies or access external services.
